app.name: ProofFlow
app.tagline: Prove your API still does what it did yesterday.

action.copyFailed: The browser would not copy it.

auth.signInSubtitle: Pick up where the last run left off.
auth.signUpSubtitle: The first account also creates a workspace.
auth.invalidCredentials: That email and password do not match an account.
auth.lockedOut: Too many attempts. Try again in a few minutes.
auth.passwordsDiffer: The two passwords are not the same.
auth.emailTaken: An account already uses that email.
auth.forgotSubtitle: Type the address you sign in with and a link will be sent to it.
auth.checkEmailBody: If that address belongs to an account, a link to choose a new password is on its way. It works once, and it expires.
auth.devLinkBody: No mail server is configured, so the link is here rather than in an inbox.
auth.reset.title: Choose a new password
auth.reset.subtitle: Ten characters or more. A phrase you can remember beats a word with a digit on the end.
auth.reset.notUsable: That link has expired or has already been used.
auth.reset.done: Your password is changed. Sign in with it.
auth.deniedTitle: You do not have access to that
auth.deniedBody: Your role in this workspace does not include this action. An owner or admin can change it.
auth.point1Body: Run an endpoint, approve the response, and ProofFlow remembers it — field by field, with the parts that change every time marked as changing.
auth.point2Body: Sign in, read a list, pick one from it, create something, check it, delete it again. Drag the steps together and pass each one's output to the next.
auth.point3Body: Not a wall of red text. Which field, what it was, what it is now, and whether that was allowed.

workspace.label: Workspace
workspace.role_TestDesigner_help: Builds and runs tests, proposes baselines.
workspace.role_Runner_help: Runs existing tests and reads the results.

project.title: Projects
project.subtitle: One project per system you test.
project.nameHint: What is this system called? For example, «Orders API».
project.descriptionHint: One line, so the next person knows what this covers.
project.accentHint: Only used to tell projects apart at a glance.
project.slugHint: Appears in links and in exported files.
project.deleteBody: Every environment, scenario, baseline and run in «{0}» goes with it. This cannot be undone.

empty.title: No projects yet
empty.body: A project holds the environments, scenarios and baselines for one system under test.

project.archiveHint: Archiving hides the project from lists. Nothing is deleted, and it can be brought back at any time.

empty.title: Nothing has run yet
empty.body: Create a project, point it at an endpoint, and the first result will appear here.

audit.title: Activity
audit.subtitle: Every change that matters, and who made it.

empty.title: Nothing recorded yet
empty.body: Changes to projects, environments, baselines and members appear here.

action.scenario.released: took a scenario out of quarantine

error.title: Something went wrong
error.body: The action did not complete. Nothing was changed.
error.404body: The link may be old, or the thing it pointed at may have been deleted.
error.403title: You do not have access to that
error.403body: Your role in this workspace does not include this action.
error.500body: The problem was recorded. Trying again is safe — nothing was half-saved.
error.invalidEmail: That does not look like an email address.

projectHome.title: This project is ready for its first environment
projectHome.body: Point it at a base URL, then run an endpoint and save what came back. Environments, scenarios and baselines all hang off this page.

environment.subtitle: One entry per place the system under test runs.
environment.newHint: Give it a name and where it lives. Everything else has a safe default.
environment.kindHint: Presentation and defaults only — the runner treats them alike.
environment.baseUrlHint: What the base-URL reference resolves to. The trailing slash is removed for you.
environment.baseUrlInvalid: That is not a complete address. It needs a scheme, like https://.
environment.maxRedirectsHint: Beyond this, a redirect is treated as a loop.
environment.allowedHostsHint: One per line. A leading *. covers subdomains but not the bare domain. Empty means only the base URL's own host.
environment.reach: What this environment is allowed to do
environment.privateNetwork.hint: Lets requests reach loopback and internal addresses. Cloud metadata endpoints stay blocked either way.
environment.invalidCertificate.hint: For a staging box with a self-signed certificate. Nothing will warn you again once this is on.
environment.isProduction.hint: A failure here is an incident. Runs ask for confirmation, and destructive cleanup refuses without an explicit opt-in.
environment.deleted: «{0}» is gone, with its variables and secrets.
environment.deleteBody: «{0}» goes, and so do the variables and secrets scoped to it. This cannot be undone.

empty.title: No environments yet
empty.body: An environment is a base URL plus the variables, secrets and limits that go with it. Most projects have one per place they deploy.

environment.productionWarning: This is a production environment. Comparing sends a real request to it.
environment.title: Environment

variable.subtitle: Values a request can refer to. Nothing here is hidden — use a secret for anything that should be.
variable.inherited.hint: Set once for the project. Editing it changes every environment.
variable.nameShape: Start with a letter or underscore, then letters, digits or underscores.
variable.deleteBody: Anything referring to «{0}» will stop resolving.

empty.body: No variables yet. Add one and refer to it from any request.

secret.subtitle: Encrypted, never shown in a list, never in an export, and masked wherever a run writes it down.
secret.unreadable: That secret could not be decrypted
secret.deleteBody: Anything referring to «{0}» will stop resolving, and the value cannot be recovered.

empty.body: No secrets yet. Add one and refer to it by name — the value is encrypted and never rendered back.

request.title: Request
request.subtitle: Build one request, send it, and look at what came back. Nothing here is saved to the project.
request.productionConfirm: «{0}» is production. Send this request against it?
request.unresolved: Some references could not be resolved, so nothing was sent.
request.unresolvedHint: A red reference does not exist in the selected environment.

noEnvironments.title: No environment to send against
noEnvironments.body: A request needs somewhere to go. Add an environment with a base URL, then come back — you can also send to a full address without one.

response.empty: Nothing sent yet. Fill in an address and press Send.
response.tooLarge: This response is too large to show as a tree without freezing the page. The raw view has all of it.

failure.Timeout: Raise the timeout in this environment's settings, or check whether the endpoint is genuinely slow.
failure.DnsFailure: Check the base URL for a typo, and that the host resolves from this machine.
failure.Refused: The server is reachable but nothing is listening on that port.
failure.Certificate: If this environment uses a self-signed certificate, allow it in the environment settings.
failure.TooManyRedirects: Raise the redirect limit in this environment's settings, or fix the loop.
failure.ResponseTooLarge: Raise the response size limit in this environment's settings.
failure.BlockedByPolicy: Add the host to this environment's allowed list, or turn on private-network reach — cloud metadata addresses stay blocked either way.
failure.Unresolved: Every reference has to exist before a request can be built.
failure.Unknown: Trying again is safe — nothing was half-sent.

baseline.subtitle: What correct looked like, and what has moved since.

empty.title: No baseline recorded yet
empty.body: A baseline is a response you have read and agreed is right. Send a request, look at what comes back, and save it.

baseline.requestHelp: Stored with the baseline so it can be sent again and compared. References are kept unresolved, so a rotated token does not break it.
baseline.noRequest: This baseline has no request stored, so it cannot be replayed.
baseline.awaitingReview: Version {0} is waiting to be approved. Until it is, comparisons still run against the approved version.
baseline.approvalNeededBySomeoneElse: Your role cannot approve a baseline.
baseline.approved: Version {0} is now the approved baseline.
baseline.nameTaken: A baseline called {0} already exists in this project.
baseline.compareExpired: That comparison is no longer being held. Compare again, then accept.
baseline.compareEmpty: Nothing compared yet. Press Compare to send the request and see what moved.
baseline.needsApproved: This baseline has no approved version yet, so there is nothing to compare against.
baseline.versionProposed: Version {0} proposed. It needs approval before it becomes the baseline.
baseline.saveAsHelp: Stores this response as what correct looks like. The request is stored with it, so the same call can be checked again later.
baseline.descriptionPlaceholder: What this response is meant to prove

diff.title: Differences
diff.invalidRules: These rules could not be read and were skipped: {0}

rule.none: No rules yet, so every field has to match exactly.
rule.help: A rule says which differences do not count. Anything without a rule has to match exactly.
rule.compareAgain: The rules changed, so the comparison on screen is out of date. Compare again.
rule.suggestionsTitle: {0} fields look like they change on their own
rule.suggestionsHelp: Nothing here is applied until you tick it and save. Each one stops a field from being checked, so read before you agree.

matcher.Exact.help: The value has to be identical to the approved one. This is what applies when no rule is written.
matcher.Ignore.help: The value is not looked at. What a timestamp or a generated id gets.
matcher.Exists.help: The field has to be there. What it holds is not checked.
matcher.NotExists.help: The field must not appear. For one that was removed on purpose.
matcher.TypeOnly.help: A string stays a string, a number stays a number. The value itself may change.
matcher.IsNull.help: The field has to be there and hold null.
matcher.IsNotNull.help: The field has to hold something — anything but null.
matcher.Regex.help: The value has to match the regular expression. For an id with a known shape.
matcher.Contains.help: The value has to contain this text somewhere.
matcher.StartsWith.help: The value has to begin with this text.
matcher.EndsWith.help: The value has to end with this text.
matcher.NumericTolerance.help: The number may differ from the approved one by up to this much. For a score that rounds differently elsewhere.
matcher.NumericRange.help: The number has to fall between these two, whatever was approved.
matcher.DateTolerance.help: The instant may differ from the approved one by up to this many seconds.
matcher.JsonSubset.help: Every approved field has to be present with the same value. Extra fields are allowed.
matcher.ArrayOrdered.help: The default for a list: first against first, second against second.
matcher.ArrayUnordered.help: The list may come back shuffled. For anything a database returns unsorted.
matcher.ArrayMatchByKey.help: Items are lined up by the field you name and then compared, so a reordered list reports what moved instead of calling every row different.
matcher.ArrayCount.help: Only the number of items is checked, against a minimum and a maximum.
matcher.CaseInsensitive.help: Compared as text, with upper and lower case treated as the same.
matcher.Trimmed.help: Whitespace at the start and end is removed before comparing.

dynamic.Timestamp: Looks like a date or a time
dynamic.TraceId: Looks like a trace or request id
dynamic.ExpiringUrl: Looks like a link that expires
dynamic.DiffersBetweenRuns: Came back different on two runs of the same request

dataset.subtitle: The inputs a test runs against, one row at a time.
dataset.nameTaken: A data set called {0} already exists in this project.

empty.title: No data set yet
empty.body: A data set is a list of inputs — two thousand identifiers, or five. Paste them in and each one becomes a call.

dataset.noKeyColumn: Without a key column, rows are identified by their position — which changes the first time the list is sorted, and re-points every approved answer at a different input.
dataset.duplicateKeys: {0} keys appear more than once ({1}…). Each input can only have one approved answer, so duplicates will be numbered apart.
dataset.blankKeys: {0} rows have no value in the key column and will fall back to their position.
dataset.versionsHelp: A version is frozen once anything has run against it. Saving edits creates the next one.
dataset.showingFirst: Showing the first {0} of {1} rows. The rest are saved and will run; a set this size is imported rather than typed.
dataset.pasteHelp: Out of a spreadsheet, a database client, or a list somebody sent you. ProofFlow works out the shape and shows you what it read before anything is imported.
dataset.noRows: Nothing here yet. Paste your inputs above, or add a row.

capture.title: Sweep
capture.subtitle: Every input, sent once, and what came back.

empty.title: No sweep yet
empty.body: A sweep sends the baseline's request once for every row of a data set, and files what comes back for review.

capture.keyboardHelp: Press j and k to move between samples, a to approve, r to reject, x to select.
capture.noResponse: This sample has no response, so there is nothing to compare.

wizard.title: Guided setup
wizard.subtitle: From an endpoint to a regression test, one question at a time.
wizard.urlHint: References in double braces are filled in per run: the environment's address, and the current row of the data set.
wizard.sendBody: Send it once and read what comes back. Come back here when the response looks right.
wizard.noBaseline: No baseline yet. Send the request, then save the response as one.
wizard.createDataSet: Create a data set from these {0} rows
wizard.sweepBody: This sends the request once for every one of the {0} rows. Nothing is approved by it — capturing records what the API does, and whether that is right is the next question.
wizard.rulesBody: If the same field differs in every sample, it is a field that changes on its own. A rule says so once, instead of you saying it two thousand times.
wizard.doneBody: Run the sweep again whenever you want to know whether anything moved. What you approved is what it compares against.
wizard.title.baseline: What does a correct answer look like?
wizard.title.data: Which inputs should it run over?
wizard.help.endpoint: The address and the method. Use double braces where a value changes per environment or per row.
wizard.help.environment: An environment carries the base address, the variables and the limits the request runs under.
wizard.help.send: Sending once, by hand, is how you find out the address is wrong before two thousand calls do.
wizard.help.baseline: A baseline is a response you have read and agreed is right. Everything later is compared against it.
wizard.help.data: One row per call. Pick a set you already have, or paste a new list.
wizard.help.sweep: This makes real calls to a real API. Nothing is approved by it.
wizard.help.review: Approve the ones that are right and reject the ones that are not. What you approve becomes the answer for that input.
wizard.help.rules: Some fields change on their own — a timestamp, a generated id. A rule stops them counting as differences.
wizard.help.done: The test exists. Run the sweep again whenever you want to know whether anything moved.
wizard.defineHelp: For a test that runs over many inputs there is no single response to save — each input has its own. This records the request; the answers come from the sweep.
wizard.noSweepYet: Go back a step and run the sweep first.

node.core.start.title: Start
node.core.end.title: End
node.http.request.title: HTTP request
node.http.request.summary: Sends a request and keeps what comes back.
node.http.graphql.title: GraphQL request
node.http.graphql.summary: Sends a GraphQL query and keeps the answer.
node.core.delay.title: Wait
node.core.log.title: Note in the log
node.core.log.summary: Writes a line into the run's log.
node.core.comment.title: Comment
node.core.comment.summary: A note pinned to the canvas. Does nothing when the test runs.
node.core.setVariable.title: Set a variable
node.core.setVariable.summary: Keeps a value under a name the rest of the run can use.
node.core.expression.title: Work something out
node.core.expression.summary: Calculates a value from what earlier steps produced.
node.core.group.title: Group
node.core.group.summary: Holds several steps together, so a long test reads as a few parts.
node.core.parallel.title: At the same time
node.core.parallel.summary: Sends several branches off at once.
node.core.join.title: Wait for the branches
node.core.join.summary: Carries on once the branches have finished.
node.core.abort.title: Stop the run
node.core.abort.summary: Ends everything now, with a reason.
node.core.checkpoint.title: Checkpoint
node.core.checkpoint.summary: Marks a place in the run, so a report can say how far it got.
node.data.extractJsonPath.title: Take a field
node.data.extractJsonPath.summary: Reads one field out of a response.
node.data.extractHeader.title: Take a header
node.data.extractHeader.summary: Reads one header out of a response.
node.data.extractCookie.title: Take a cookie
node.data.extractCookie.summary: Reads one cookie out of a response.
node.data.extractRegex.title: Find with a pattern
node.data.extractRegex.summary: Pulls a piece out of some text using a pattern.
node.data.extractStatus.title: Take the status code
node.data.extractStatus.summary: Reads the response's status code as a number.
node.data.jsonParse.title: Read as JSON
node.data.jsonParse.summary: Turns text into something the other steps can look inside.
node.data.jsonStringify.title: Write as text
node.data.jsonStringify.summary: Turns a document back into text.
node.data.mapFields.title: Rename fields
node.data.mapFields.summary: Builds a new document with the fields you name.
node.data.filterList.title: Keep some of a list
node.data.filterList.summary: Drops the items that do not match.
node.data.sortList.title: Sort a list
node.data.pickIndex.title: Take one item
node.data.pickIndex.summary: Takes the item at a position in a list.
node.data.count.title: How many
node.data.count.summary: Counts the items in a list.
node.data.merge.title: Put two together
node.data.template.title: Build some text
node.data.template.summary: Puts values into a sentence you write.
node.data.datasetRow.title: The current input
node.data.datasetRow.summary: The row of the data set this iteration is running against.
node.data.generate.title: Make a value up
node.data.generate.summary: Produces an id, a name, an email — something to send.
node.data.base64.title: Base64
node.data.hash.title: Hash
node.assert.status.title: Check the status code
node.assert.status.summary: Fails unless the response came back with the code you expect.
node.assert.header.title: Check a header
node.assert.header.summary: Fails unless a header says what you expect.
node.assert.jsonField.title: Check a field
node.assert.jsonField.summary: Fails unless a field in the response is what you expect.
node.assert.jsonSchema.title: Check the shape
node.assert.jsonSchema.summary: Fails unless the whole response has the shape you described.
node.assert.responseTime.title: Check how long it took
node.assert.responseTime.summary: Fails if the response took longer than you allow.
node.assert.bodyContains.title: Check the body contains
node.assert.bodyContains.summary: Fails unless the response holds this text somewhere.
node.assert.listCount.title: Check how many
node.assert.listCount.summary: Fails unless a list has the number of items you expect.
node.assert.listContains.title: Check a list contains
node.assert.listContains.summary: Fails unless a list holds an item with this value.
node.assert.notNull.title: Check it is there
node.assert.notNull.summary: Fails when a value is missing or empty.
node.assert.matchesRegex.title: Check it matches a pattern
node.assert.matchesRegex.summary: Fails unless the text matches the pattern.
node.baseline.compare.title: Compare with the baseline
node.baseline.compare.summary: Fails when the response differs from what was approved.
node.baseline.capture.title: Record as a baseline
node.baseline.capture.summary: Files this response as what correct looks like.
node.test.softFail.title: Record a problem
node.test.softFail.summary: Notes something wrong without stopping the run.
node.test.expectFailure.title: This should fail
node.test.expectFailure.summary: Holds steps that are meant to fail, and complains if they pass.
node.test.tag.title: Tag the run
node.test.tag.summary: Adds a label a report can group runs by.
node.test.attach.title: Attach something
node.test.attach.summary: Keeps a value with the run, so a reader can see it later.
node.flow.if.title: If
node.flow.if.summary: Takes one path or the other.
node.flow.switch.title: Choose a path
node.flow.switch.summary: Takes one of several paths, by value.
node.flow.forEach.title: For each item
node.flow.forEach.summary: Runs what is inside once per item of a list.
node.flow.forEachRow.title: For each input
node.flow.forEachRow.summary: Runs what is inside once per row of a data set.
node.flow.repeat.title: Repeat
node.flow.repeat.summary: Runs what is inside a set number of times.
node.flow.while.title: While
node.flow.while.summary: Keeps going while a condition holds, up to a limit.
node.flow.break.title: Leave the loop
node.flow.break.summary: Stops the loop it is inside.
node.flow.continue.title: Next time round
node.flow.continue.summary: Skips the rest of this pass through the loop.
node.flow.retry.title: Try again
node.flow.retry.summary: Runs what is inside again when it fails.
node.flow.pollUntil.title: Keep checking
node.flow.pollUntil.summary: Runs what is inside until a condition holds, or time runs out.
node.flow.tryCatch.title: Try, and if it fails
node.flow.tryCatch.summary: Runs what is inside, and takes another path if it goes wrong.
node.flow.cleanup.title: Clean up
node.flow.cleanup.summary: Runs at the end whatever else happened — for undoing what the test created.
node.flow.rateLimit.title: Slow down
node.flow.rateLimit.summary: Keeps what is inside under a number of calls a second.
node.flow.skipIf.title: Skip if
node.flow.skipIf.summary: Passes over the next steps when a condition holds.
node.auth.basic.title: Basic authentication
node.auth.basic.summary: Signs requests with a username and password.
node.auth.bearer.title: Bearer token
node.auth.bearer.summary: Signs requests with a token you already have.
node.auth.apiKey.title: API key
node.auth.apiKey.summary: Adds a key to every request, in a header, the address or a cookie.
node.auth.oauth2ClientCredentials.title: OAuth2 client credentials
node.auth.oauth2ClientCredentials.summary: Gets a token using a client id and secret.
node.auth.oauth2Password.title: OAuth2 password
node.auth.oauth2Password.summary: Gets a token using a username and password.
node.auth.oauth2Refresh.title: OAuth2 refresh
node.auth.oauth2Refresh.summary: Exchanges a refresh token for a fresh one.
node.auth.login.title: Log in
node.auth.login.summary: Posts credentials and takes the token out of the answer.
node.auth.setHeader.title: Use the token
node.auth.setHeader.summary: Puts a token on every request from here on.
node.auth.cookieJar.title: Cookies
node.auth.cookieJar.summary: Keeps or clears the cookies the server sent.
node.auth.signHmac.title: Sign it
node.auth.signHmac.summary: Makes a signature from a payload and a secret.
node.core.delay.help: Real time, on whatever runs the test.
node.core.expression.help: A small expression, not a program. ProofFlow runs other people's tests, so it does not run arbitrary code.
node.data.datasetRow.help: Leave empty to use the set the loop around this is walking.
node.test.expectFailure.help: Say why, so the next reader knows this is deliberate.
node.flow.cleanup.help: The reason this exists: a test that creates a record has to delete it even when an assertion in the middle failed.

nodeprop.url.help: Use {{environment.baseUrl}} for the part that changes per environment.
nodeprop.timeout.help: Leave empty to use the environment's limit.
nodeprop.scope.help: A run, or just the current pass through a loop.
nodeprop.title: Title
nodeprop.maxConcurrent.help: Fewer is kinder to the API on the other end.
nodeprop.wait.help: All of them, any one, or whichever finishes first.
nodeprop.name: Name
nodeprop.path.help: Click a field in a response to fill this in without typing it.
nodeprop.pattern.help: A regular expression. The part in brackets is what is taken.
nodeprop.mapping.help: On the left the new name, on the right where to take it from.
nodeprop.index.help: Counting from zero, so the first item is 0.
nodeprop.seed.help: Give it a word and the value stops changing between runs — which is what a baseline needs.
nodeprop.expectedStatus.help: One code, several separated by commas, or a family like 2xx.
nodeprop.schema.help: A JSON Schema. Describes what the response must look like.
nodeprop.soft.help: The failure is recorded and the run keeps going — useful when one step checks fifteen things.
nodeprop.sampleKey.help: For a test that runs over many inputs, which one this answer belongs to.
nodeprop.approve.help: Off by default, and worth leaving off: a capture that approves itself is a test that can never fail.
nodeprop.redact.help: Attachments end up in reports people forward.
nodeprop.cases.help: On the left the value, on the right which path it takes.
nodeprop.maxIterations.help: A ceiling, always. A loop with none is a run that never ends.
nodeprop.limit.help: Useful for trying a scenario against ten rows before all two thousand.
nodeprop.concurrency.help: How many inputs are in flight together.
nodeprop.cacheToken.help: Otherwise every request asks for a new token.
nodeprop.tokenPath.help: The field in the answer that holds it.
nodeprop.headerScope.help: Everything after this, or only this branch.
nodeprop.cookieAction.help: Keeping them is what makes a session work across steps.

canvas.nothingSelected: Select a step to see what it does and change it.
canvas.disable: Leave it out of the run
canvas.unknownType: A kind of step this version does not know
canvas.oneStartOnly: A scenario begins in one place, and it already has one.

scenario.subtitle: Tests drawn as a picture of what happens.
scenario.nameTaken: A scenario called {0} already exists in this project.
scenario.cannotPublish: A scenario with problems in it cannot be published.

empty.title: No scenario yet
empty.body: A scenario is a test drawn as a picture: send a request, check the answer, do something about it if the answer is wrong.

graphProblem.noStart: This scenario has no starting point, so nothing would run. Add a Start.
graphProblem.twoStarts: There is more than one starting point. A run has to begin somewhere in particular.
graphProblem.noName: This step has no name, so nothing else can refer to what it produced.
graphProblem.duplicateName: Another step is already called «{0}». References like {{steps.{0}.response}} would not know which one you meant.
graphProblem.unknownType: This step is of a kind this version of ProofFlow does not know («{0}»). It may come from a newer version.
graphProblem.danglingEdge: A connection points at a step that is no longer here.
graphProblem.unknownPort: A connection between «{0}» and «{1}» uses a socket that no longer exists on one of them.
graphProblem.portKindMismatch: «{0}» and «{1}» are joined in a way that mixes the order steps run in with the values they pass along.
graphProblem.missingInput: «{0}» needs something plugged into it before it can run.
graphProblem.unreachable: Nothing leads to «{0}», so it would never run.
graphProblem.cycle: The connections come back round to «{0}», so the run would never finish. Use a Repeat or a Keep checking step to go round on purpose.

run.title: Run
run.graph.empty: This run has no graph to show.
run.cancel.title: Stop this run?
run.cancel.body: It stops at its next step. Any cleanup steps still run, so what the test created is still removed.
run.empty.title: No runs yet
run.empty.body: Open a scenario and run it. What happened will be here afterwards, step by step.

matrix.subtitle: The same tests, at the same moment, in more than one place.
matrix.cannotStart: This project needs at least one scenario and one environment first.
matrix.ceiling: Every cell is a real request to a real API.
matrix.empty.title: No matrix has been run yet
matrix.empty.body: Choose some scenarios and two or more environments, and the grid will show where each one passes.
matrix.onlyOneSide: Only one side reached these steps:
matrix.noSharedSteps: These two runs share no step that returned a response.

schedule.subtitle: What runs on its own, and when.
schedule.zone.hint: «Every morning» means morning here. Written as an IANA name, like Asia/Tehran.
schedule.cron.hint: Five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.
schedule.delete.title: Delete this schedule?
schedule.delete.body: It stops running. The runs it already started are kept.
schedule.empty.title: Nothing runs on its own yet
schedule.empty.body: A suite nobody remembers to run is a suite that finds problems late. Add a schedule and it will tell you.

cron.zone: That time zone is not known here.
cron.nothingToRun: Everything it covered has been deleted.

flaky.title: Tests that cannot make up their minds
flaky.subtitle: The same test, the same version, the same environment — passing sometimes and failing others.
flaky.none: Nothing here is flaky, over the last fortnight.
flaky.reason: Too unreliable to fail a build on.

apikey.title: Keys
apikey.subtitle: What a build agent uses to start a run.
apikey.list.subtitle: Revoked keys stay listed, so the trail still names them.
apikey.none: No key has been issued for this project.
apikey.name.hint: Name it after what will hold it, so revoking is obvious later.
apikey.expiry.hint: A key that never expires is a real choice. A key that does is the better one.
apikey.revoke.title: Revoke this key?
apikey.revoke.body: Anything using it stops working immediately. It cannot be undone.
apikey.issued.title: Here is the key. This is the only time it is shown.
apikey.issued.body: Nothing here stores it — not this page, not the database. Copy it now, or issue another one later.
apikey.howto.body: Start a run, wait for it to finish, then fetch the report your build system already reads.

approval.notAllowed: Approving is not something your role does.
approval.notYourOwn: You recorded this one. Somebody else has to approve it — that is what makes the review mean anything.
approval.title: Waiting on a decision
approval.subtitle: Everything in this project somebody has to look at.
approval.empty.title: Nothing is waiting
approval.empty.body: Every recorded answer has been decided about.
approval.versions.subtitle: A whole response recorded, waiting to become the one runs compare against.
approval.sessions.subtitle: Captured samples nobody has decided about yet.

team.subtitle: Who is in this workspace, and what each of them may do.
team.members.subtitle: Roles decide what somebody sees and what they may change.
team.notYourself: Your own role is not yours to change.
team.noSuchMember: That person is not in this workspace.
team.lastOwner: The last owner cannot be removed or demoted — the workspace would have nobody to repair it.
team.remove.title: Remove this person?
team.remove.body: {0} loses access to this workspace. What they made stays.
team.role.change.title: Change this role?
team.role.change.body: {0} can currently do {1} things. The new role decides the rest.
team.invite.roleHint: Start narrow. A role is easier to widen than to take back.
team.invitations.subtitle: Sent but not taken up yet.
team.invite.link.title: Here is the link. Pass it on yourself.
team.invite.link.body: No mail server is configured, so nothing was sent. Only a hash of this link is stored, so this is the one time it is shown.
team.invite.sent: An invitation is on its way to {0}.

mail.failed: The mail server would not take the message.
mail.reset.subject: Choose a new ProofFlow password
mail.reset.body: Somebody asked to reset the password on your ProofFlow account. Follow the link to choose a new one.
mail.reset.ignore: If that was not you, nothing has changed and you can ignore this. The link works once and expires.
mail.invite.subject: You are invited to {0} on ProofFlow
mail.invite.body: {0} has invited you to the {1} workspace on ProofFlow. Follow the link to join with the account you sign in with.
mail.invite.ignore: If you were not expecting this, you can ignore it. Nothing happens until you follow the link.

portability.export.subtitle: This project as a file you can keep in a repository.
portability.export.secrets: No secret is in this file.
portability.export.secrets.body: Not the value, not the encrypted form of it. The names travel so whoever imports it knows what to create; the values stay here. Open the file in an editor and see for yourself.
portability.export.contents.subtitle: Runs, activity and rejected proposals are not — they are the record of what happened here, not the description of the tests.
portability.export.file.body: No date in the name, on purpose: exporting again replaces the last one, which is what makes the history readable.
portability.import.subtitle: A ProofFlow file, or somebody else’s.
portability.import.upload.help: JSON or YAML, up to 16 MB.
portability.import.paste.help: A cURL command copied from a browser’s network panel goes here.
portability.import.asNew.help: Leave this off and everything is added to «{0}».
portability.import.look: Look at what it would do
portability.source.proofflow.help: Exported from this product, here or anywhere else.
portability.source.openapi.help: Version 3, JSON or YAML. One scenario per operation.
portability.source.postman.help: A v2.1 collection. Scripts are not carried across.
portability.source.curl.help: One command, as your browser’s network panel copies it.
portability.preview.title: Before anything happens
portability.preview.subtitle: Nothing has been written yet. This is what pressing the button would do.
portability.preview.counts: An import only adds. Nothing already here is changed or replaced.
portability.preview.skipped: Already here, and left exactly as they are:
portability.preview.secrets: You will have to create these yourself
portability.preview.secrets.body: The file names them but does not carry their values. Until they exist, anything that uses them will fail.

import.tooLarge: That file is too big to import.
import.notYaml: That is not YAML this can read.
import.notABundle: That is JSON, but it is not a ProofFlow export.
import.tooNew: That file was written by a newer version of ProofFlow than this one.
import.noSuchProject: That project is not here any more.
import.noUrl: That command has no address in it.
import.notOpenApi: That is not an OpenAPI document.
import.swagger2: That is Swagger 2, which is a different format. Convert it to OpenAPI 3 first.
import.notPostman: That is not a Postman collection.
import.postmanV1: That is a Postman v1 collection. Export it again as v2.1.
import.noRequests: That collection has no requests in it.
import.unknownSource: That is not something this can read.
import.expired: That file is no longer held. Choose it again.
import.note.basicPassword: The password from -u was not kept. Create a secret called «password».
import.note.cookie: A cookie was found and not kept — cookies are a session, not a setting.
import.note.insecure: The command switched off certificate checking. That is a decision about an environment, so it was recorded rather than applied.
import.note.unknownFlag: A flag this does not know was skipped.
import.note.getWithData: -G moves the data into the query string. Check the address before running it.
import.note.manyServers: The document lists more than one server. The first one was used.
import.note.noExampleBody: An operation has a body but no example, so it arrived empty. A body invented from a schema is a guess that looks like a fact.
import.note.nonJsonBody: An operation sends something other than JSON. Its body did not come across.
import.note.tooManyOperations: The document has more operations than one import will take. The rest were left.
import.note.tooManyRequests: The collection has more requests than one import will take. The rest were left.
import.note.scripts: Pre-request and test scripts were not carried across. ProofFlow does not run script from a file.
import.note.fileBody: A request sends a file from somebody’s machine. Nothing useful crosses.
import.note.oauth2: An OAuth2 token was found and not kept — it is somebody’s live session.
import.note.unknownAuth: An authentication kind this does not know was skipped.

template.title: Templates
template.subtitle: Twelve scenarios to start from. Choosing one writes a real graph you can change.
template.needsChoosing: Pick a data set or baseline before it will run.
template.smoke.title: Is it up
template.smoke.summary: Ask the health endpoint, check it answers, check it answers quickly. The one that runs every hour.
template.notFound.title: Something that is not there
template.notFound.summary: Ask for a record that does not exist and check the refusal is a 404. An API that returns 200 and an empty object is broken in a way no positive test notices.
template.listThenDetail.title: A list, then one of them
template.listThenDetail.summary: Read a list, take an identifier out of the first item, and read the thing it names.
template.signIn.title: Sign in and use the token
template.signIn.summary: Post credentials, keep the token, and call something that needs it.
template.crud.title: Make it, read it, delete it
template.crud.summary: The whole life of one record, ending with a check that it is really gone.
template.baseline.title: Compare against a baseline
template.baseline.summary: Call an endpoint and compare the whole answer with what was approved.
template.dataDriven.title: Once per row
template.dataDriven.summary: The same request repeated for every row of a data set.
template.pagination.title: Page by page
template.pagination.summary: Walk a list three pages deep, checking each page as it comes.
template.pollJob.title: Start it, then wait for it
template.pollJob.summary: Kick off something slow and ask until it is ready, rather than sleeping and hoping.
template.retry.title: Allowed to fail twice
template.retry.summary: A step that gets three attempts with a growing pause between them.
template.validation.title: Send something wrong
template.validation.summary: Post an invalid payload and check the refusal names the field that was wrong.
template.cleanup.title: Tidy up afterwards
template.cleanup.summary: Make something, test it, and take it away again whatever happened.

retention.label: Keep response bodies and logs for
retention.help: What a run decided — passed or failed, how long it took, which checks held — is kept for ever. This is about the bulk: the bodies each step produced, the log lines and the artefacts. Those are what make a database grow without limit, and what is most likely to still hold somebody's personal data long after anybody needed it.
retention.cleared: The bodies and log for this run have been cleared.
